messages:
maya (Finance): Heads-up — Acme Analytics just flagged a CA sales tax line on their latest invoice and want it removed. They say Redwood should be the marketplace facilitator, so we should not be charging sales tax. Can tax/legal weigh in?

jordan (Tax): Quick Qs: is this for hosted API usage only or for a partner model billed through us? Marketplace facilitator rules typically apply to marketplace sellers, not SaaS usage. Need details.

maya (Finance): It's hosted API usage + one line called "Model Marketplace – Partner-XL". We invoice Acme directly (no passthrough). Invoice snippet below:

```
Invoice #R-87213
Bill to: Acme Analytics, 412 Market St, San Jose, CA 95113
Line items:
 - Hosted API compute (usage) ................ $2,350.00
 - Model Marketplace – Partner-XL (usage) ... $1,200.00
Subtotal .................................. $3,550.00
Sales Tax (CA) 1.4% .......................... $49.70
Total ...................................... $3,599.70
```

maya (Finance): Customer sent back a tax notice requesting credit for the $49.70.

lee (Product Ops): For Partner-XL we surface partner models but we run inference on our infra and bill customers on our invoices. Not a multi-vendor checkout.

sam (Legal): @maya thanks for the snippet. If we control billing and delivery, we are usually the seller of record. Some states still treat marketplace facilitation differently, but CA mostly taxes tangible personal property; SaaS is mixed. Need to check if Partner-XL is treated as taxable tangible property or a nontaxable service.

jordan (Tax): I ran a quick check. CA typically does not broadly tax SaaS subscriptions, but there are carve-outs depending on bundled taxable software or prewritten software delivered electronically. The "marketplace facilitator" argument feels off because we invoice and collect. However — if Partner-XL contains third-party deliverables or license transfers, that could change treatment.

taxbot: Automated lookup: California CDTFA guidance: tangible personal property and certain prewritten software may be taxable. No blanket CA marketplace-facilitator exemption for invoiced sellers. (ref: https://www.cdtfa.ca.gov/).

maya (Finance): Acme's tax team insists their reseller rules apply because the partner provided the model weights. They say Redwood simply lists it in UI. They asked for a credit while they gather more info.

jordan (Tax): Action items: 1) get partner contract language re: license transfer vs hosted inference, 2) confirm whether Partner-XL line includes any one-time license fees or just usage, 3) ask Acme for their tax determination memo.

sam (Legal): We can provisionally issue a one-time credit for the CA tax amount while we research, to preserve customer relations. Approval required from finance lead. Document decision as a credit memo and flag for tax audit.

maya (Finance): Requesting approval to issue $49.70 credit to Acme pending follow-up. I'll tag the credit as provisional and attach supporting ticket.

sam (Legal): Approved for provisional credit up to $50. Please add note: "Provisional credit issued pending tax classification review; reversible if classification changes."

lee (Product Ops): I'll pull the partner contract and confirm license vs hosted inference by EOD.

jordan (Tax): I'll do a deeper CA tax analysis and circle back with legal. If we conclude taxable, we'll keep the tax and explain. If not, finalize credit and update billing logic to avoid future tax.

maya (Finance): Thanks all. I'll issue the provisional credit now and add the credit memo to the ticket. @taxbot — please save the CDTFA links in the tax-op citelog. :thumbsup:

taxbot: Saved CDTFA refs and created ticket TAX-1456 for CA marketplace/SaaS review.
